glosses: to sickle (to cut with a sickle)
An implement having a semicircular blade and short handle, used for cutting long grass and cereal crops.

examples.text:
Lou's not Times foole, though roſie lips and cheeks
VVithin his bending ſickles compaſſe come,
Loue alters not with his breefe houres and vveekes,
But beares it out euen to the edge of doome:
If this be error and vpon me proued,
I neuer vvrit, nor no man euer loued.

Oft did the harveſt to their ſickle yield,
Their furrow oft the ſtubborn glebe has broke;
How jocund did they drive their team afield!
How bow’d the woods beneath their ſturdy ſtroke!

glosses: A sickle faether, any of the sickle-shaped rear feathers of the domestic cock.

examples.text:
Then, ere the silver sickle of that month
Became her golden shield, I stole from court
With Cyril and with Florian, unperceived.

glosses: Of red blood cells: to assume an abnormal crescent shape.

examples.text: Even the cells of heterozygotes will sickle if the oxygen tension is low enough.

glosses: To deform (as with a red blood cell) into an abnormal crescent shape, to cause to sickle.
